claims.text: Introducing a controlled volume fraction of stable nanoscale dispersoids into a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature and irradiation-exposed mechanical performance without compromising thermal or irradiation stability.
The baseline refractory high-entropy alloy has a coarse or unrefined microstructure typical of this alloy class.
Carbide or oxide nanoparticles can be incorporated as a tailored dispersion in the alloy matrix.
The selected carbide or oxide nanoparticles will remain thermally and irradiation stable in the alloy matrix.
Performance should be evaluated above approximately 800°C.
Dispersoid particles will pin grain boundaries.
Dispersoid particles within grains will hinder dislocation motion.
The dispersoids will promote grain refinement.
Dispersoid-mediated obstruction of dislocations will produce particle-dispersion strengthening.
Dispersoids will suppress grain growth at high temperature.
The dispersoid-modified alloy will maintain phase stability under irradiation.
The dispersoid-enhanced alloy will have greater high-temperature yield strength than the unmodified alloy.
The dispersoid-enhanced alloy will have better high-temperature creep resistance than the unmodified alloy.
The dispersoid-enhanced alloy will have thermal stability similar to that of the unmodified alloy.
The dispersoid-enhanced alloy will have irradiation stability similar to that of the unmodified alloy.
The proposed effects require chemical compatibility between the refractory high-entropy alloy and the selected dispersoid.
Unfavorable reactions between the dispersoids and matrix may prevent the proposed effects.
